# DE-SynPUF Legacy Source: Profiling Findings and Data Quality Rules

**Source:** CMS DE-SynPUF Sample 1 (2008–2010), legacy claims system of the acquired plan
**Profile report:** `docs/profiling/desynpuf_profile.md` (generated by `ingestion/legacy/profile_desynpuf.py`)
**Status:** v2, open questions resolved by bronze investigations (`sql/investigations/02_*`, `03_*`); drives the source-to-target mapping and silver-layer validation

## Volumes

| File | Rows | Columns | Grain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Beneficiary Summary 2008 | 116,352 | 32 | One row per member per year |
| Beneficiary Summary 2009 | 114,538 | 32 | One row per member per year |
| Beneficiary Summary 2010 | 112,754 | 32 | One row per member per year |
| Inpatient Claims 2008–2010 | 66,773 | 81 | One row per claim segment |
| Outpatient Claims 2008–2010 | 790,790 | 76 | One row per claim segment |

Member counts decline about 1,800 per year (death or disenrollment). Members who leave must remain in the member dimension so historical claims still resolve.

## Findings and rules

| # | Finding | Evidence | Rule | Layer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | `CLM_ID` is not unique; claims are split into segments | Inpatient: 68 repeated `CLM_ID`s; Outpatient: 10,975. `CLM_ID + SEGMENT` unique in both | Grain is one row per claim segment; natural key `CLM_ID + SEGMENT`. Claim-level metrics aggregate segments by `CLM_ID` | Bronze, Silver |
| F2 | Negative payment amounts | `CLM_PMT_AMT` negative: 55 inpatient, 2,566 outpatient. `MEDREIMB_IP`/`MEDREIMB_OP` negatives in all beneficiary years | Retain as adjustments; flag `is_adjustment = true`; include in all financial control totals | Silver, Reconciliation |
| F3 | Diagnosis codes stored in procedure columns | Inpatient `ICD9_PRCDR_CD_2`–`_6` only 47–48% match ICD-9 procedure format; failures are diagnosis codes (e.g., V5866, E8889, 25000, 41402). `ICD9_PRCDR_CD_1` 100% valid | Validate each code against the code system its column claims. Misplaced values go to `quarantine.code_exceptions` with reason `WRONG_CODE_SYSTEM`; never loaded as procedures | Silver |
| F4 | Corrupted HCPCS values (~0.03%) | `201E5` (scientific-notation corruption), `0851`/`0841`/`0521` (4-digit revenue codes), `TOTAL`, `DIALY`, `520`, `108` | Route to `quarantine.code_exceptions` with reason codes `SCI_NOTATION`, `REVENUE_CODE`, `NON_CODE_TEXT`, `TRUNCATED`. Claim line retained; invalid code not loaded | Silver |
| F5 | Placeholder primary diagnosis | Outpatient `ICD9_DGNS_CD_1` = `OTHER` in ~0.7% of populated rows | Set code to null, flag `primary_dx_missing = true`; claim retained | Silver |
| F6 | Outpatient ICD-9 procedure columns effectively empty | `ICD9_PRCDR_CD_1`–`_6` 99.97–100% null in outpatient | Not mapped to silver (outpatient procedures come from HCPCS). Retained in bronze for audit | Silver |
| F7 | Yearly beneficiary snapshots | `DESYNPUF_ID` unique within each yearly file | Build `dim_member` as SCD Type 2 across 2008–2010 snapshots | Silver, Gold |
| F8 | Repeating code groups stored wide | `ICD9_DGNS_CD_1`–`_10`, `ICD9_PRCDR_CD_1`–`_6`, `HCPCS_CD_1`–`_45` | Unpivot to `claim_diagnosis` and `claim_procedure` (long format) with `sequence_num`; sequence 1 = principal diagnosis | Silver |
| F9 | Sparse secondary diagnoses | e.g., inpatient `ICD9_DGNS_CD_10` 91.8% null | Expected; nulls dropped during unpivot, not treated as errors | Silver |
| F10 | Text reading preserves codes | All values read as text; leading zeros intact (e.g., `0389`) | All codes and IDs typed as text end to end; never cast to numeric | All |
| F11 | Segment 2 rows are continuation records with no dates but real payments | Segment 2: 68 inpatient / 11,253 outpatient rows, 0 with dates; paid $1,277,700 inpatient and $15,232,360 outpatient; 5,656 outpatient segment 2 rows carry diagnoses | Segment 2 inherits dates and header attributes from segment 1 of the same `CLM_ID`. Claim total paid = sum of all segments. Diagnoses from all segments are unpivoted | Silver |
| F12 | Orphan continuation segments | 278 outpatient segment 2 rows have no segment 1 (paid $392,320); 0 inpatient | Quarantine with reason `ORPHAN_SEGMENT`; dollars included in reconciliation (bronze = silver + quarantine) | Silver, Reconciliation |
| F13 | Claims starting in 2007 | 224 inpatient and 312 outpatient claims start Nov–Dec 2007; all end in 2008 | Claim year and enrollment matching use the **thru (end) date**, not the start date | Silver |
| F14 | No orphan members once year logic is correct | Using thru-date year on segment 1: 0 of 846,242 claims lack enrollment in that year; 0 members never seen | Referential check `claim → member enrolled in claim year` is enforced as a test that must stay at zero | Silver, Tests |
| F15 | Claim IDs unique across claim types | 0 `CLM_ID`s shared between inpatient and outpatient | `CLM_ID` is globally unique within this source; silver key still includes `source_system` to stay unique once EDI and FHIR claims arrive | Silver |
| F16 | No service after death | 0 claims with service date after recorded death | Payment-integrity check kept as a recurring test | Tests |

## Validation design constraints

1. **Date-aware code validation.** Claims are from 2008–2010; reference files are current (HCPCS Oct 2026, ICD-10-CM FY2027). Validating historical codes against current sets would falsely reject codes retired since then. ICD-9 diagnosis codes are validated against the ICD-9 code list in the 2018 GEMs (`2018_I9gem.txt`); HCPCS Level II codes are validated using effective/termination dates where available.
2. **HCPCS Level I (CPT) codes.** The CMS HCPCS file contains Level II codes only. CPT codes are AMA-licensed and are validated for format only, never against descriptions.
3. **Exceptions never disappear.** Every rejected value lands in a quarantine table with source file, row key, column, original value, and reason code, and is counted in reconciliation.

## Resolved questions

| Question | Answer | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Do segments of one claim span different members or dates? | Never different members. Segment 2 has **no** dates at all, so it cannot conflict; it inherits from segment 1 | `02_bronze_open_questions.sql` Q1b; `03_segment_followup.sql` F1 |
| Do `CLM_ID`s appear in both inpatient and outpatient? | No (0 overlap) | Q2 |
| Claims for members not enrolled that year? | None, once claim year uses the thru date and segment 2 rows are excluded | Q3, F3, F4 |

## Lesson recorded: validate the validation

The first segment check (Q1b) reported "0 segments differ by date." That result was misleading: `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)` ignores NULLs, and every segment 2 row has NULL dates, so a dated and an undated segment looked consistent. Likewise, the first orphan check reported 11,857 claims ($19.5M) without enrollment; the true number was 0. Both were caught by cross-checking totals (segment 2 rows = null-date rows exactly; "not enrolled" minus null-date rows = 2007-start claims exactly). Investigation queries are now checked against an independent total before their results become rules.
